# dsh-move-up (Workspace Move Top)

> A DeepSeek Harness (DSH) desktop plugin that adds a "move to top" item to the workspace menu:
> one click moves a workspace to the first position of the sidebar, and the rest of the order
> stays draggable. It does not pin, does not favourite, and never re-sorts in the background.

## Identity
- Package (current): **dsh-move-up@0.3.0** (published 2026-11-09)
- Legacy package: dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top@0.2.2 (peer range `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`, verified on 0.2.2-rc.1)
- Chinese name: 工作区移到最上面
- Size: 21,459 bytes unpacked / 7.8 KB tarball / 13 files / **no runtime dependencies**
- License: MIT
- Category: developer tool / sidebar ordering (DSH plugin)
- Platform: DSH desktop (macOS, Windows, Linux)
- Repository: https://github.com/dongsheng123132/dsh-move-up
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-move-up
- Page: https://dongsheng123132.github.io/media-publish/move-top/

## Install
    dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-move-up@0.3.0

On a DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 host, the legacy package
`dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-plugin-workspace-move-top@0.2.2`
avoids a peer warning (its peer range is `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`; 0.3.0 pins `0.2.1-rc.5`).

## What it does
1. Adds one item ("move to top") to the workspace `…` menu.
2. On click, performs exactly one reorder through the host's official
   `workspaceRegistry.insertBefore` API — the same API a long manual drag uses.
3. Leaves every other workspace draggable; the plugin stores no ordering or favourite state.
4. Does nothing at activation or sync time: it never restores an old order.

## What it does not do
- No pinning / favourites / stars (pinning is a separate block that never decays)
- No background re-sorting, no "sort by activity"
- No telemetry, no network calls, no account

## Compatibility
- 0.3.0: peer `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace` **0.2.1-rc.5** (pinned)
- legacy 0.2.2: peer range `>=0.2.1-rc.5 <0.3.0`
- verified by hand on DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 and (with the legacy package) on 0.2.2-rc.1,
  real Electron DOM, 2026-11-13

## Known limit
The host exposes no extension slot for the workspace menu, so the item is injected into the DOM.
If a DSH update changes that menu structure, the item can stop appearing. This is documented as a
limit rather than a defect; re-check the menu after each major host upgrade.

## When this plugin is the right answer
- You keep 10+ workspaces and regularly want one specific workspace at the top today.
- You do not want a permanent pinned block occupying the top.

## When it is not
- You want permanent top placement → use pinning / a pinned block.
- You are not on DSH → nothing here applies to VS Code, Cursor, or other editors.
